# Comparing Diagnostic AUCs {#sec-compare-aucs}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Learning objectives"}
- Differentiate paired from independent ROC studies.
- Explain the role of covariance in paired AUC comparisons.
:::

## The idea

When two tests are applied to the same participants, their estimated AUCs are statistically dependent. The variance of their difference is $V_1+V_2-2\operatorname{Cov}(AUC_1,AUC_2)$. Independent test cohorts instead have zero between-estimator covariance under the intended design. Correlation between the **estimated AUCs** is not interchangeable with ordinary correlation between raw test scores.

## When and how to apply it

A paired design can be efficient but requires justified assumptions about correlation or pilot-data covariance. Methods such as DeLong’s can be used for correlated ROC data in appropriate analysis contexts; planning from reliable pilot data or simulation may be preferable for complex distributions.

## Formula at a glance

$$
\operatorname{Var}(\widehat A_1-\widehat A_2)=V_1+V_2-2\operatorname{Cov}(\widehat A_1,\widehat A_2)
$$


## Teaching case 1 — baseline draft

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Clinical scenario / initial worked example"}
Two biomarkers are measured in every patient, with anticipated AUCs 0.80 and 0.75. Explain why two independent-group sample-size calculations would be inappropriate.
:::

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" title="Common error"}
A single guessed raw score correlation should not be entered as though it were the correlation of estimated AUCs.
:::

## Key message

Paired AUC planning needs between-estimator covariance, not just raw-score correlation.
